dish: Hand-tossed scratch-made pizza (plus hoagies and wings) — voted Erie's best pizza 14 years running
w: Serving Edinboro and Erie since 1979, John's Wildwood won Best Pizzeria in Erie Reader's 2025 Best of Erie (over runners-up Ippa and Valerio's) and has topped local pizza rankings for well over a decade — Erie's benchmark scratch pizza, hoagie and wing shop.

dish: Creole shrimp & andouille sausage over grits — Haitian-Southern fusion
w: Chef Jean Paul, born in Port-au-Prince and trained from Chicago to NYC, fuses Haitian technique with Southern soul food; the shrimp & grits and seared catfish have made it one of Erie's most talked-about tables and a fixture on lists of Pennsylvania's beloved Black-owned restaurants.

dish: Wood-fired Neapolitan margherita from an 800-900° brick oven, with house-made cheese
w: Owner Jason Spore trained in Italy and fires true Neapolitan pies (and a signature white pizza) in a brick oven inside the Flagship City Food Hall; a runner-up for Best Pizzeria in Erie Reader's 2025 Best of Erie and a fixture on locals' best-pizza lists.

dish: Birria tacos with consommé, and fresh-never-frozen Angus smash burgers
w: Started in 2021 as an Erie food truck slinging birria tacos, now a brick-and-mortar smash-burger-and-birria joint that won Erie Reader and Erie's Choice Best Food Truck awards and drew a WICU/WSEE feature; a cult local favorite for its Cooper-cheese smash burgers and quesabirria.

dish: Honey jerk chicken thighs over coconut rice and red beans
w: Family-owned Caribbean spot that grew from a food truck outside a Valu Home Center into a State Street storefront; its sticky-sweet, spicy honey jerk chicken was singled out in Erie Reader's 2026 'Can't Miss Dishes,' and its opening drew Erie News Now coverage.

dish: Gourmet Smith's-wiener hot dogs (the Yinzer, the Chicago dog) with 300+ beers
w: A quirky Route 97 bar-and-grill (open since 2011) serving 32 gourmet takes on the local Smith's wiener alongside 300-plus draft, craft and bottled beers; a repeat Best of Erie finalist (Best Sandwich Shop 2019, Best Local Business 2021) across from Presque Isle Downs.

dish: Mushroom toast — roasted umami mushrooms and lemony ricotta on sourdough; braised meats and hand-cut steaks
w: Erie-native chef Aaron Bush, formerly of Cork 1794, opened this west-side New American room in 2025; its mushroom toast made Erie Reader's 2026 'Can't Miss Dishes,' anchoring a menu of braised meats and scratch sides.

dish: Crispy dry-style chicken wings, including the signature Bleu Hot blend
w: A no-frills Fairview roadhouse west of Erie whose crispy dry-style wings are a perennial pick in Erie Reader's wing polls and local readers' 'best wings' lists — a favorite of locals and Lake Erie fishermen alike.

dish: Soft-serve twist cones and 'snowstorms'; the Twinkle Kote (sprinkles + candied peanuts)
w: A seasonal Chestnut Street soft-serve stand serving Erie since 1965 and a summer institution — dipped cones, candy-loaded snowstorms and the nostalgic Twinkle Kote — celebrated in a dedicated GoErie photo retrospective.

dish: Ten independent kitchens under one roof — Dominican mangú, Neapolitan pizza, Brooklyn bagels, Syrian shawarma
w: Erie's first food hall, opened 2021 as part of the EDDC's $100M downtown revitalization in the former Park Place/Sherlock's buildings; about ten independent vendors (Ippa Pizza, Dina's Dominican, Jo's Brooklyn Bagel, Khir Damascus, CheesErie and more) plus a bar and 160+ seats.

dish: Mangú (mashed plantains) with 'The Two Hits' — fried cheese and Dominican salami
w: Run by John and Dina Csir out of the Flagship City Food Hall, bringing Dina's homeland Dominican recipes — mangú, fried cheese and salami, stewed chicken — to downtown Erie; a fast-growing cult favorite among the food hall's vendors.

dish: Soup flight — three daily house-made soups with a trio of locally sourced breads
w: A locally-sourced specialty grocery and cafe from No Dirt Farms owner Amanda Hines, with hydroponic produce growing in the room; its soup flight made Erie Reader's 2026 'Can't Miss Dishes' and pairs with the market's toasty sandwiches.
